📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that meta has justifiably attracted more scrutiny than ever this year, along with multibillion-dollar judgments and settlements, over how its business practices affect young social media users.
  • In fact, the tech giant has made a major push toward drawing teenagers to one of its flagship platforms, Instagram, by targeting them at their schools.
  • According to documents obtained and reported by NPR, Meta launched an initiative called Project Gryffindor, named after a Hogwarts house in the Harry Potter series, to create school communities on Instagram in order to boost user counts and engagement on the platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that meta has justifiably attracted more scrutiny than ever this year, along with multibillion-dollar judgments and settlements, over how its business practices affect young social media users. The company, however, is not retreating.

In fact, the tech giant has made a major push toward drawing teenagers to one of its flagship platforms, Instagram, by targeting them at their schools.

According to documents obtained and reported by NPR, Meta launched an initiative called Project Gryffindor, named after a Hogwarts house in the Harry Potter series, to create school communities on Instagram in order to boost user counts and engagement on the platform.

Recent findings suggest that meta’s goal of approaching young users where they spend the most time offline was not a secret. As recently as late September, the manufacturer said it was expanding its School Partnership Program, which includes 17,000 schools, with a stated goal to “help students and parents stay informed.”.

The company’s internal documents reveal some of the motivations behind Meta’s push for school adoption and Project Gryffindor’s proposed features, such as school banners on teen profiles and the ability to search school directories by class year. The details were acquired as part of discovery in a multistate lawsuit over whether social media platforms are designed to be addictive to consumers under 18. Meta is a defendant in the case, along with other companies, including TikTok, Snap and Google.

In 2024, Instagram introduced Teen accounts and has since been trying to assure parents they’re safe while rolling out additional protections. Studies, however, have suggested that young teens regularly encounter unsafe content or deal with unwanted contact. Recruiting more owners at an early age without resolving these risks could make teens more vulnerable to mental health challenges and increase the chances of being bullied or harassed.

A representative for Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Sources indicate that to anyone familiar with Meta’s long history of privacy oversteps on platforms like Facebook, the documents aren’t surprising. They reveal a company primed to give school-age children newly introduced ways to chat and connect with each other, and to encourage them to bring their friends along, expanding Instagram’s user base and engagement.

Like other social platforms, Instagram primarily makes its money from targeted advertising. User retention is a key part of Meta’s strategy.

In one of the document slides, titled “Why schools, why now?” which preceded Gryffindor’s launch, Meta stated, “Competitors are exploring school social use cases, but IG may be better positioned for school connections thanks to our differentiator of meeting new people and building relationships with acquaintances.” In other words, Instagram’s size and scale, with about 3 billion active consumers globally, automatically make it a draw for students.

The NPR report comes within a week of a filing against Meta alleging that it’s withholding evidence in a major case involving social media’s effects on teenagers.

One of Meta’s marketing pitches for its School Partnership Program is that it’s trying to create online safe spaces for students, while giving parents and schools more oversight on what’s accessible on the platform. But experts warn that Meta’s history makes it hard to trust the company with protecting kids from predators or scammers.

Katie Paul, director of the Center for Accountability’s Tech Transparency Project, which has been researching how Meta handles child-safety complications, noted that Instagram Teen accounts “are not safe as advertised” and that nothing is “legally requiring the manufacturer to make these safe.” Paul pointed out that Instagram debuted these accounts only when lawsuits over social media harm started rolling in.

“It’s all part of a broader marketing (effort) to claim that these are just safer for kids because they are Teen accounts,” Paul said. That marketing effort has included paid endorsements from therapists, psychologists and parent influencers to promote Teen accounts. The case for building up partnerships with schools is a way of “passing the buck on responsibility” to schools and parents, Paul said.

Parents, in particular, have less power in Instagram’s school groups: Unlike the school administrators tasked with managing school groups, parents have no powers to moderate or manage those groups; they can only view them. For Teen accounts in general, parents can’t view direct messages sent to or received by their children.

Meta’s business interests in its push for student engagement and school partnerships are easy to see through. Because kids are likely to be lifetime users on these platforms, getting them hooked early has long-term financial value.

“Ultimately, Meta is the one profiting off of the data collection of these kids while simultaneously failing to keep them safe,” Paul said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

Recent findings suggest that if it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions.

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:.

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Sources indicate that software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

In a recent development, instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s upcoming.

Industry observers note that what comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”.

According to recent reports, in other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving tech giant labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your manufacturer needs a chief AI officer in 2026.

I find it particularly telling that this is from the tech giant that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

Recent findings suggest that that’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

In a recent development, microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the tech giant’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the tech giant’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:.

This means the manufacturer doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

The torch in AI has been passed.

Nvidia had been the stock market's avatar for AI since the launch of ChatGPT, but with Anthropic now becoming the first AI lab to go public, it's set to take over as the market's best reflection of AI sentiment.

Industry observers note that anthropic is a pure-play AI organization founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees who thought that company was too weak on safety. Anthropic builds AI models and software products based on its frontier intelligence platform, Claude.

According to recent reports, anthropic's IPO also gave the manufacturer a chance to have the investing world's full attention, and CEO Dario Amodei spoke for about five minutes at the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday, sharing his vision for the company. Here are three things investors should know about the newly public company, direct from Amodei.

According to recent reports, dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

Anthropic has made its prioritization of safety clear from its inception, and AI safety has only become more salient amid concerns of AI models going rogue, escaping sandboxes, and the intensifying competition with China.

Anthropic's emphasis on safety may also be a competitive advantage at a time when AI is facing a backlash. The midterm elections reflected growing discontent with data centers and could lead to a slowdown or increased restrictions on them, at least in some states.

The emphasis on safety also acts in the company's interest in terms of liability and reputational damage, as the future of AI is wide open and will be determined by companies like Anthropic.

Amodei told the audience, "There's a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety, and an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic's DNA from the start.".

Amodei wants everyone, including investors, customers, and AI skeptics, to know that he's one of the good guys.

In a similar vein, Amodei described a best-case scenario for the AI competition as a "race to the top.".

Amodei stated, "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful manufacturer, others will be inspired to do the same.".

In a recent development, if that spirit takes hold in the industry, then, he remarked, everybody wins, no matter who has the best models. Amodei assured investors that they intend to lead that race, saying, "The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.".

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Amodei began his comments with a story about how his father died of a disease, Hepatitis C, that was cured just a few years later.

The event clearly showed Amodei the power of invention and new technology, and after beginning his career in biology, he moved over to artificial intelligence, where he sees the potential for tremendous breakthroughs in medicine and beyond.

The departure of Jensen Huang due to a scandal involving multiple affairs is a reminder of the importance of character in leadership, and Amodei seems to possess that sufficiently.

In a recent development, anthropic is a mission-driven company and the rare public benefit corporation on the stock market. Amodei brings a deep commitment to that mission and a personal passion for research and intelligence that can cure diseases and solve humanity's most pressing problems.

In a recent development, in its new iPadOS 27.3 release, Apple is adding several new features for iPads — Siri mode in the camera app, window resizing by tapping and more tools in the Freeform whiteboard app. The features are being tested in beta and will be released to the general public sometime in December. The new OS will be available on all iPads that support iPadOS 27.

The release notes for iPadOS 27.3 are listed here.

You can also take action items, such as pointing the camera at a restaurant bill and asking Siri to split it if you want to split it with people you’re with.

Recent findings suggest that that same functionality will soon be available on iPads, with the iPadOS 27.3 release. Maybe you want to identify a plant out in nature, or an historic building during a walking tour, or figure out how to replicate a tasty dish you just ordered at a restaurant.

Prior to the iPadOS 27.3 release, you had to drag a corner of the window to make it bigger or smaller.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption.
  • During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella revealed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
  • Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella revealed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several latest Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

Industry observers note that “As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft noted. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft stated, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s upcoming Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft noted the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft noted.

It has been revealed that the manufacturer added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

According to recent reports, nadella also declared a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. At the moment in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft mentioned of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

Microsoft also revealed that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can swiftly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft confirmed a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

According to recent reports, agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the manufacturer’s observability platform. Microsoft mentioned Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft indicated how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft mentioned. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

GTA 6 Launch Day Hits Different for Fired Rockstar Workers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1134 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration.
  • For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.
  • It has been revealed that “I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” indicates Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration. But not everyone who worked on the cultural juggernaut is joining the victory lap.

For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.

It has been revealed that “I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” indicates Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland. “But it’s impossible because of how much hurt the firing has caused everyone.”.

Rockstar fired the workers on the spot — something that’s only legal in the UK in cases of gross misconduct — alleging that they’d shared confidential firm information on a Discord server.

The workers tell a different story. They say the company had long been aware of the Discord server, and only fired them when it started to look as though their efforts to unionize might succeed. They believe they were made an example of.

On the evening before the game’s launch, I spoke with Yordanova and her former colleague Dayne Oram, a senior production coordinator who had been at Rockstar for seven years and was also affected by the dismissals, about how they were feeling about launch day.

In a recent development, “One of our fellow colleagues remarked it the best,” says Yordanova. “What we’ll feel tomorrow is mourning what could have been, whether we want to or not.”.

For all those who are mourning, others among the fired workers still hold a candle for GTA. Jacob Jones, who spent one year as a game tester before taking a role as a designer on the open world team for four years, was raring to play the game on launch day.

Jones graduated from being a childhood fan of the franchise – even counting the signatures of Rockstar co-founders Sam and Dan Hauser among his merch collection – to his dream job. He remains a GTA fan to this day, but describes feeling a sense of “poignance” and “bittersweetness” toward the launch.

For Oram, Yordanova and Jones, GTA 6 eve was already a heavy day, even aside from the launch fever.

Recent findings suggest that they’re all part of a case brought by the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain on behalf of 23 former Rockstar North employees, who say they were unfairly dismissed for union activity. Hours before Oram and Yordanova spoke with me, a Glasgow employment tribunal had heard Rockstar’s closing submissions, which now leaves the fired workers in limbo as they wait for a verdict.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar North maintains that it fired the employees for gross misconduct. The tech giant didn’t respond to a request for further comment.

Industry observers note that oram, Yordanova and Jones all speak highly of their former colleagues and teams, but Oram calls the sacking a “traumatic experience.” Only Yordanova managed to secure alternative employment in the past 13 months. Jones claims for now he’s focused on getting justice.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, reminders of their former employer have been everywhere as the studio geared up to release perhaps the most highly anticipated game of all time. Billboards, buses and online ads have been impossible to avoid, leaving Yordanova feeling “devastated.”.

It has been revealed that “I’ve genuinely had to make sure to avoid looking at it,” she says. “It’s such a cool game, and to know that you worked on it, you feel a sense of pride and joy to see it out. But it’s like that sense of joy has been taken away from us in such a ruthless manner.”.

Oram acknowledges having “mixed feelings” about the launch. It’s been fantastic watching video footage of people playing and reviewing the game, they say. At the same time, they’ve found it difficult not being able to celebrate the moment with their former team.

Sources indicate that the workers fired from Rockstar North had varying ideas about whether they wanted to celebrate the launch, or avoid it entirely. Jones is one of those who started playing the game as soon as he got home from the tribunal at 1 a.m. By the time we spoke on Thursday, he’d played around six or seven hours.

“I personally think it’s a masterpiece,” he notes. Even though he worked on the game, he’s discovering surprises everywhere. “I haven’t completed it yet, but I do think it is probably the greatest game ever made.”.

According to recent reports, oram states that they planned to stick with watching streams of the game on launch day. “I’m probably not going to play the game for a little while, but I am looking forward to at least watching some people,” they say. Oram worked across so many bits of the game that there’s plenty they’re excited to see people discover.

Yordanova states she’s firmly in the avoidance camp. “I was really excited about playing the game in its official form because obviously when you work on it, you get to play it,” she says. “Even while we were in the office, there were parts I was really excited about – but I don’t think I’ll be playing it for the foreseeable future.”.

It has been revealed that she hopes that one day her feelings will change, she adds. “But right now, that’s just not possible in any way.”.

It has been revealed that instead, she’ll be spending the day with friends who supported her over the last year. She aims to “dive into another art form” by seeing the stop-motion animated film Wildwood at the cinema, which particularly appeals to her as a lighting artist.

Many people playing GTA 6 around the world won’t be aware of what happened to Oram, Yordanova, Jones and their colleagues during the game’s development, but the affected workers would like people to know. “I understand people just want to focus on the joy, but I don’t think you can separate the launch with what happened,” says Yordanova.

Reflecting on what happened, Jones says it’s such a shame the way things went down. “It was my absolute passion,” he says. “I just wish that the circumstances were different, and I would have loved to have still been there working on games. I wish I got to the end.”.

Industry observers note that correction, Nov. 20: An earlier version of this article stated that none of the three fired Rockstar workers had secured further work, which is not the case.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the manufacturer.
  • Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the manufacturer. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

Recent findings suggest that “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, stated during the keynote.

In a recent development, the approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft stated it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman mentioned during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

Industry observers note that the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the firm has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman noted of the new coding model the manufacturer announced at Ignite.

In a recent development, the company also released its upcoming image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

Our Readers Say This Is the Laptop Brand to Shop for During Black Friday Sales

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums.
  • Recent findings suggest that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics.
  • It has been revealed that apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple people saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a latest laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

Recent findings suggest that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you plan to buy a new laptop while there are holiday savings.

It has been revealed that apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple people saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

Apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

How much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple users paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” stated Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

If you plan to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — right now MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

It has been revealed that apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple customers said their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

Digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple customers seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

Take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple people may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

Battery life is a big deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) noted their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook users saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

According to recent reports, comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo customers say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test reveals that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

Apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its owners either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

“Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” said Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

Industry observers note that the fresh MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook users have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.

According to recent reports, and MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple owners reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their problems. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.

Our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.

In a recent development, “Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” said Goldman.

In a recent development, lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it notes encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.

When it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple users reported poor performance.

Recent findings suggest that here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without issues or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.

Recent findings suggest that on the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple users rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.

Apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple users planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.

Usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.

Sources indicate that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

According to recent reports, I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is presently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

Recent findings suggest that this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
  • Sources indicate that A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov.
  • Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

Sources indicate that A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

Back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

An Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

Industry observers note that apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and people. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

When news of the shutdown spread, Apple users flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

Recent findings suggest that for many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

In a recent development, in discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community owners to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others stated the site grew less helpful over the years.

CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he said.

Industry observers note that just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

In a recent development, the shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push users away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

According to recent reports, reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual consumers to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

Apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The manufacturer may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum consumers on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

Whatever the reason, the circle of Apple users helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar plans.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how rapidly it can drain.

In a recent development, even if you haven’t played a video game since Frogger, it’s tough to ignore Thursday’s launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, the most preordered video game of all time. Some companies gave employees a day off to play. (CNET bosses, I’d like the same for the next Animal Crossing game, OK?).

Recent findings suggest that mcDonald’s launched a promotion that lets GTA 6 players order burgers and fries via Discord without stopping the game. And CNET’s Andrew Lanxon played it for 24 hours straight at his Edinburgh home, much to his ignored cat’s dismay.

Naturally, the memes and jokes are revved up. I’ve never played any of the Grand Theft Autos, and I still laughed at these.

Many of the memes play off a common complaint about how long it took the much-anticipated GTA 6 to arrive: 13 years.

“We got [fill in the blank] before GTA 6” was the usual caption.

We deadass got a whole fresh ocean before GTA 6 https://t.co/dE9MVty8js.

The Marvel Mania account went one step further and listed as many things as possible that “we got” before GTA 6, including COVID-19, a new English king, foldable phones, a second Donald Trump presidency, an American pope, McDonald’s Grimace shake, the Hawk Tuah meme, the Roman Empire trend and many more.

People immediately started looking for a new long-awaited item to fill GTA 6’s place in the meme. George R.R. Martin’s eternal Game of Thrones sequel, yer up!

Now it just goes back to "We got ______ before George RR Martin's THE WINDS OF WINTER".

GTA 6 might be fun for players, but not for the fictional cops in the game. Minnesota’s South St. Paul Police Department was one of several actual law-enforcement agencies that got in on the release hype, posting: “Our thoughts are with the Vice City Police Department tonight as they prepare for an influx of visitors.”.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 includes 34 types of cats and dogs you can pet, as well as other animals. If you spend any time on social media, you know cats are a favorite pick. This post jokes about coaxing the little furballs with the “pspsps” sounds.

Recent findings suggest that sure, you can do wild, crazy things in GTA 6, but you can also… grocery shop? Numerous memes have poked fun at a screenshot noting that Lucia “will appreciate” it if you bring home groceries.

Wrote one Bluesky user, “I think I’m going to spend all my time in GTA6 fixing up the house, buying groceries, raiding gang hideouts, feeding my pet. Total escapism from life where I can barely afford any of that.”.

In a recent development, I think I’m going to spend all my time in GTA6 fixing up the house, buying groceries, raiding gang hide outs, feeding my pet. Total escapism from life where I can barely afford any of that.

The American Heart Association got in on the release hype by telling veteran players they’re old.

“If you’ve played GTA on more than one console generation, it’s time to get your cholesterol checked,” one post read. Thanks a lot, Mom.

If you're calling in sick to play GTA VI, you need to schedule your annual visit. pic.twitter.com/sxHAh7wvZs.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.
  • Salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents.
  • In a recent development, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

Salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

In a recent development, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a upcoming brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Industry observers note that retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

Industry observers note that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

The majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

Industry observers note that retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

Today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

    Uber Is Testing Rides for Kids With Qualified Drivers

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (428 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids.
    • The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
    • On the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The new program expands on the manufacturer’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which introduced in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

    The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole new influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

    On the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

    First off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

    As any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

    According to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

    According to recent reports, live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

    Uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

    An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

    Breaking: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting.
    • Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.
    • In a recent development, openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid intends, which start at $20 per month.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

    Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

    In a recent development, openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid intends, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

    If Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The firm already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

    Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

    Sources indicate that abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

    Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

    During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

    At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent customers may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

    AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

    Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

    Recent findings suggest that as with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

    The feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US users can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

    The change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The upcoming landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

    “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

    AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

    In a recent development, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

    “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release mentioned. Google’s new Memory summary feature for Gemini lets people view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

    #51011. Latest Update: 11 Steps I Use for Quick Smart Home Prep for Guests and Holiday Visitors

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1196 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: 11 Steps I Use for Quick Smart Home Prep for Guests and Holiday Visitors

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1196 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over.
    • Sources indicate that if you have holiday or event intends involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices.
    • Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over. Since I test home security and multiple smart devices, I tend to have a lot. But they don’t have to be a distraction when you have visitors staying over. On the contrary, smart tech can usually help out.

    Sources indicate that if you have holiday or event intends involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices. These changes save me headaches and time, while impressing guests. You may even decide to enable some features year-round.

    Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.

    Doorbell chimes are just the start of your smart guest experience.

    Recent findings suggest that video doorbells often come with a feature in settings to switch to seasonal themes, including a variety of holiday sounds for the end of the year. Vivint is particularly good at this, equipping its video doorbell with options for many different holiday songs. Google Nest doorbells and Eufy doorbells also have holiday options.

    Smart lighting is easy to set up for certain times of day, dimming and brightening as necessary.

    Recent findings suggest that cameras and guests don’t play well together. Help everyone feel safe by pulling down the shutters on your indoor cameras, nanny cams and smart displays (or disabling them through settings, etc.). Let everyone know their privacy is secured while staying over. Video doorbells and outdoor cams are fine to leave functioning, especially if you want to keep an eye on kids going crazy in your backyard.

    Recent findings suggest that today’s smart lights include options to turn on at certain times of day or at sunrise, and at a specific brightness (and even color temperature). Some even allow you to gradually increase the brightness over an hour or so. Use these settings to set a simulated sunrise in key spots of the house to encourage guests to rise and shine at the right times. It’s especially handy if everyone needs to be up in the morning for a special activity — but make sure to provide coffee too.

    Aqara’s app distills a whole lot of smart lock options into a highly digestible product card.

    Recent findings suggest that A smart lock allows for all kinds of tricks, like remote operation and auto-locking if it’s left unlocked. Those work great when you have guests over, but if you want to add even more options, many locks allow you to create temporary passes — including through common apps like Apple Home — and send them to your guest’s phones. That way they can come and go on their own schedules, and the door stays locked when no one is using it.

    Today’s smart thermostats, including the Google Nest, have humidity sensors, too.

    Keeping the thermostat triggering temperatures a bit low in winter is a great way to save energy, but not always the sign of a good host. Consider heading into your thermostat app and bumping up temperatures a few degrees, especially at night and the middle of the day, so everyone stays comfortable. The latest models can even sense humidity, which can be notable if guests are sensitive to very dry or very wet air.

    ADT’s newly introduced hub has a few extra tricks.

    Home security system schedules usually call for arming the system during the day after everyone has left the house. That doesn’t work so well over the holidays, especially if you have guests over. Instead of disabling individual sensors, we suggest setting your home security system to disarm during the day.

    It has been revealed that you can still get key alerts from devices like leak detectors or package-recognizing video doorbells with the system disarmed. And you can leave the night mode armed (which usually lets people move around but monitors doors and windows closely).

    It has been revealed that A guest Wi-Fi network is an excellent add-on if you have multiple people coming to visit. It lets you set a separate network and easy-to-remember password for all guest devices, keeping your home network safer and letting you prioritize key home devices. Plus, you can keep reusing it whenever people come over in the future. We’ve got a full guide on how to set a guest network up, but it’s usually very easy with app settings.

    Prep your smart speakers for guests to avoid any problems.

    Smart home speakers like an Echo or the latest Apple HomeView are excellent devices for playing holiday music for a whole house. But there’s a small problem: With a lot of extra guest devices on your Wi-Fi, music streaming may not be reliable. You can solve this problem by downloading a playlist to a device like a phone or tablet and playing it on the smart speaker via Bluetooth. Many common apps like Spotify let you do this, especially if you have a subscription.

    It has been revealed that voice assistants are handy and fun, but they can be a distraction when others are around, especially if kids start getting creative in their commands. You could turn voice assistants off entirely, but we like the option to limit what they can do.

    In a recent development, for example, Alexa has a Voice ID section in its settings that allows you to limit skills and third-party services from working with any voice except the profiles you create and add for you and direct family members. Google Assistant has a very similar option with its Voice Match settings, which limits device controls to only certain voices.

    It’s also a good idea to set up a voice code to confirm any purchases made over voice assistants, so people can’t buy something with just a command.

    A wireless charger nearly anyone can use.

    With the ubiquitous Qi charging standard, wireless chargers can work with nearly any phone. Make things easier for your guests by setting out a wireless charger or two for them to use without managing a tangle of power adapters. Bonus points if you offer chargers that have multiple charging pads, sparing your outlets even more.

    In a recent development, if you have a little extra time, most home security systems can connect to compatible smart lighting and let you create routines to make them more useful. Specifically, we’ve had great results creating night mode routines for security sensors that turn on nearby smart bulbs at low brightness settings when motion is detected.

    This way, if someone gets up in the middle of the night, they can have a soft light to help them find their way without disturbing anyone else.

    It has been revealed that don’t have a home security system? You don’t need one: Devices like this $50 Philips Hue motion sensor work independently and can automatically tell smart lights what to do when someone approaches.

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:07PM EST.

    Nvidia's terrible month just got worse.

    It has been revealed that shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting. The drop erased roughly $491 billion in market value in a single session, taking Nvidia from about $3.52 trillion to about $3.03 trillion.

    It has been revealed that zoom out and the damage is even bigger. Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6. At Friday's price, the stock is down about 48% from that high, and the company has lost about $2.7 trillion in value in just six weeks.

    Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.

    The Wall Street Journal first reported on Tuesday that the SEC was investigating Nvidia but couldn't say what the probe was about. On Friday, Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, reported that the agency's enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at the company.

    Recent findings suggest that many questions remain unanswered. Reuters couldn't determine when the inquiry began or which accounting practices are under review. The SEC declined to comment, and Nvidia didn't immediately respond. Keep in mind that the SEC investigates plenty of companies that are never charged with anything.

    The stock was already having a bad day before the report: shares were down more than 6% earlier in the session amid a broad sell-off in AI stocks.

    Industry observers note that the probe adds to a pile of problems. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 11 following revelations about his personal relationships, including with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China, which China denies. The Justice Department is also reviewing Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face, according to Reuters.

    Recent findings suggest that two areas could draw scrutiny. The first is how Nvidia reports where its sales come from. The manufacturer breaks out revenue by where customers are headquartered, rather than where they're billed. On that basis, about 63% of last quarter's revenue came from U.S.-based customers. The Financial Times has reported that Nvidia made the switch as sales billed to Singapore approached half of its total, a bad look with Southeast Asia having become a hub for chips smuggled into China.

    In a recent development, the second is how Nvidia helps its customers pay for its chips. On Tuesday's earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia's guarantees totaled $118 billion at the end of the quarter, including $105 billion of credit support tied to a single data center campus. These guarantees are the kind of disclosure the SEC is watching closely at AI companies. When a chipmaker helps fund the projects that buy its chips, it's harder to tell how much demand would exist on its own.

    In a recent development, none of this has shown up in the numbers yet. Nvidia's revenue jumped 103% to $115.8 billion last quarter, and the manufacturer expects about $130 billion this quarter. Management even raised its growth forecast for next fiscal year to about 75%. At about $126, the stock trades at roughly 12 times last quarter's adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share on an annualized basis, cheap for a company growing this fast.

    It has been revealed that but cheap can get cheaper. Accounting questions hit at the heart of what investors pay for: trust in the numbers. Until Nvidia names a permanent CEO and the SEC's focus becomes clearer, the stock could stay volatile, even after a 48% drop.

    For long-term investors who already own Nvidia, there's no need to panic-sell on a report about an investigation. For anyone thinking of buying, it's smarter to wait for more clarity, or to build a position slowly, than to bet that the worst is over. There are plenty of other semiconductor stocks without a cloud of investigations hanging over them.
