    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • Industry observers note that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    Industry observers note that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    Sources indicate that you can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Sources indicate that stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Sources indicate that despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    Sources indicate that I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    In a recent development, there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    It has been revealed that for breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    According to recent reports, if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    Industry observers note that for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    Industry observers note that for a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    Industry observers note that one of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    Sources indicate that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, ONEOK (OKE -2.48%) raised its full-year financial guidance for the third time this year after reporting record natural gas processing volumes in the Permian Basin region of West Texas and New Mexico. A debt paydown and an integrated pipeline footprint give the company room to fund growth projects while returning capital to shareholders.

    Three things management stated stand out.

    The company paid off nearly $5.5 billion of debt during the third quarter after completing a $9 billion equity transaction. Management is using that balance sheet relief to shift its leverage target to 3.25 times debt-to-EBITDA or lower, where EBITDA represents earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a metric measuring core operating profitability.

    In a recent development, total raw feed throughput for natural gas liquids (NGLs), which are liquid hydrocarbons such as propane and ethane, grew 6% year over year. The company stored raw feed while waiting for its Medford fractionator facility to restart in mid-December, pushing those associated earnings into early 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that surging power demand from electric utilities and technology data centers is driving long-term commitments for natural gas pipeline capacity. ONEOK recently locked in a 10-year contract to move 250 million cubic feet per day of natural gas to power a 1-gigawatt plant.

    Producer drilling activity is building across the Bakken and Mid-Continent regions, giving management direct momentum into year-end. ONEOK's integrated network connects wellhead gathering to Gulf Coast export facilities, protecting cash flow through long-term fee contracts and active commodity hedging while management tracks drilling discipline and regional pricing differentials.

    With debt paydowns opening up balance sheet room and recent acquisitions adding Permian scale, ONEOK is positioning its system to capture expanding power generation and export demand.

    Sources indicate that there are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel intends than the groupings suggest.

    Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

    » Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

    Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

    According to recent reports, they’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

    You can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel prepares before choosing.

    Each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

    Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

    Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

    Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

    Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

    Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

    Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

    Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

    Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

    Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

    Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

    Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

    The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

    It has been revealed that fresh lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

    Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

    Industry observers note that global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    If PCE demonstrates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes.     I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though.     If I Could Tell All S&P 500 Investors Just 1 Thing Right Now, It's This

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.
    • Sources indicate that at one point in 2025, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) fell 19% below its high.
    • In 2020, the index dropped by nearly 35% during the COVID pandemic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Dierking – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

    Sources indicate that at one point in 2025, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) fell 19% below its high. It still finished the year up 16%.

    In 2020, the index dropped by nearly 35% during the COVID pandemic. It also closed out the full calendar year with a gain of 16%.

    In 2026, stocks are sliding again. Right now, the S&P 500 sits about 6% below its all-time high, but the Nasdaq-100 is down nearly 13%.

    I don't tell you this to suggest that U.S. stocks are poised for a rapid recovery like they experienced earlier this decade. It's to tell you that episodes like this are part of the experience when investing in stocks.

    If you own the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%), here's the one thing I'd tell you right now. These declines are no doubt painful, but they're the price of admission when accumulating long-term wealth.

    Here's an interesting bit of stock market trivia. Since 1980, the average intra-year drop in the S&P 500 has been 14.2%. But despite this, the S&P 500 has produced a positive calendar-year return in 35 of those 46 years.

    In other words, market corrections are a normal and regular occurrence for the S&P 500. But so are the recoveries from them. And the fact remains that stocks spend much more time rising than they do falling. The short-term losses are part of the path to long-term gains.

    One of the most underrated moves an investor can make is making no move at all.

    When stock prices are falling, many people rush to sell their stocks, fearing that more losses are on the way. They may say something like they're going to wait for things to get "better" before they get back in.

    There are a couple of things wrong with that thinking.

    In a recent development, first, selling stocks after they've fallen only locks in the loss. It doesn't erase it. Second, stock market rebounds are often well underway by the time investors feel that things have gotten "better.".

    In a recent development, the sum total of these actions means that a lot of folks lock in the loss, miss out on the rebound, and end up damaging their long-term returns. If the S&P 500's long-term annualized return is around 10%, the average investor usually ends up getting less than that.

    That's why the one thing I like to tell investors is: Get used to the stock market's volatility. It's normal and it's a daily occurrence. Corrections of 10% or more are fairly frequent and should be expected from time to time. It's how you handle them that makes the difference. If you can buy and hold instead of giving in to the temptation to sell, you have a better chance of reaching your financial goals.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1397 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • Recent findings suggest that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's key to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • Recent findings suggest that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    Recent findings suggest that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's key to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    Recent findings suggest that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    Sources indicate that these scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    In a recent development, merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    According to recent reports, merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    Some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that demonstrates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Recent findings suggest that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    Recent findings suggest that some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    It has been revealed that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    It has been revealed that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    Scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    Which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    Industry observers note that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Recent findings suggest that scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    It has been revealed that the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    Think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a big impact when you add several of them together.

    It has been revealed that understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    It has been revealed that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    #50934. Industry News: How To Teach Your AI Agent About Your Firm

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (791 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: How To Teach Your AI Agent About Your Firm

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Frederik Riskær Pedersen, Founder and CEO of Maplith, a tech giant brain for your AI agents.
    • For 16 years, I ran a translation company that grew from a handful of people into an international business.
    • In a recent development, one customer shows it well.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Frederik Riskær Pedersen, Founder and CEO of Maplith, a tech giant brain for your AI agents.

    For 16 years, I ran a translation company that grew from a handful of people into an international business. The most vital thing I learned about knowledge is that it rarely lives where you think it does.

    In a recent development, one customer shows it well. We had to fetch their files from their own system and deliver them in their own layout, and we could only invoice some of the repetitions. None of that was written down anywhere. It lived with one project manager. Anyone else would have done it the standard way and got it wrong.

    That tailoring was not a side issue. It was the product. If the work had been standard, the customer could have run the model themselves. This is why a tech giant’s rules never get standardized away: The exceptions are often exactly what customers pay for.

    I think of this every time someone asks me why their AI agent isn’t delivering. The models are good enough. The problem is that the agent starts from zero every time. It does not know which systems you run, how they connect or which rules you follow without ever writing them down. So it guesses, and a confident guess in your accounts is worse than no answer at all.

    Industry observers note that here are five things you can do this month before you let an agent work inside your business. None of them needs a upcoming tool.

    It has been revealed that book two hours with the three or four people who make most of the everyday decisions. Ask them one question: “What would a upcoming hire ask you in their first week?” The answers are your unwritten rules: which customers get special terms, when a refund is approved, what can be invoiced and what cannot. Write each one as a short sentence, specific enough to check: “This customer gets files back in their own template.” “Refunds above 300 euros are approved by the finance lead.”.

    List every system you use and what each one is the source of truth for. You will find places where two systems describe the same thing differently. “Returned” in the ERP can mean the customer has sent the item back, while in the warehouse it means the item is back on the shelf.

    According to recent reports, the instinct is to make the systems agree. In my experience, that rarely works because each system was set up for the team that uses it, and that is why it works for them. Write the translation down instead. The same goes for numbers. In my company, the price did not sit in the same place from one customer to the next. Note where it lives for whom and which value to trust for which question.

    Most useful answers need two systems joined: the order in the web shop and the invoice in accounting, or the support ticket and the customer in the CRM. Find the field that ties them together and test it by hand. Take 20 random orders and look for them in the other system. If you find 19, you can build on that link. If you find 12, you cannot, and an agent will rarely tell you it is guessing. The test takes an afternoon and saves months of wrong reports.

    Recent findings suggest that split actions into four levels: read, propose, act after approval and act alone. Start with everything that changes something requiring approval from a named person. Set limits in money and volume, not in trust. When the agent has proposed the same action a hundred times without a mistake, move that one action up a level. That decision should be yours, never the agent’s.

    For every action, record who asked for it, who approved it, what happened and when. It sounds bureaucratic, but it is the only way to answer when a customer, an auditor or your board asks, “Why did this happen?” Without a log, you also cannot tell when it is safe to give the agent more freedom.

    Recent findings suggest that none of this is about artificial intelligence. It is about making knowledge that lives in people’s heads, and in systems that do not talk to each other, available and trustworthy. Companies that do this get more out of their AI. They also become less fragile when a key person goes on holiday or leaves.

    Recent findings suggest that so start small. Book the two hours this week, write down 10 rules and test one link.

    #50928. Industry News: Trust Is The Newly introduced Battleground For Customer Engagement

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (934 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Trust Is The Newly introduced Battleground For Customer Engagement

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.
    • ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult.
    • Every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.

    ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult. Amid the meteoric rise of AI-enabled scams, call spoofing and social engineering attacks, the challenges organizations face when trying to reach consumers seem insurmountable.

    Every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage. Many of the traditional warning signs consumers were trained to recognize have disappeared—consumers are on edge.

    And with good reason: It’s a jungle out there.

    Sources indicate that in our recent global study, “61% of business leaders ranked fraud among the risks with the greatest potential business impact, ahead of cybersecurity breaches, compliance, customer churn, operational cost and reputational risk. More concerning, 58% said they’re very or extremely concerned fraud is evolving faster than their organizations’ abilities to detect and prevent it.”.

    Historically, organizations have viewed fraud and engaging with customers as separate disciplines. But today’s threat environment makes it clear they’re deeply interconnected. In many cases, the communication channel itself—whether a phone call, text message, email or mobile app interaction—provides the first indication that fraud may be occurring.

    According to recent reports, consumers don’t experience fraud, identity and communication challenges as separate issues. To them, it’s one experience, one problem. It’s a trust problem that’s reshaping the customer journey. In fact, 69% of consumers say they would switch vendors for stronger security.

    Trust has become the foundation for both customer engagement and fraud prevention.

    Industry observers note that at our recent Fraud & Communications Summit in Chicago, keynote speaker Matt O’Neill, a former U.S. Secret Service Special Agent and recipient of Gold and Silver Awards for distinguished service, shared insights from years spent working undercover as a banker, broker, money launderer and other personas. In these roles, he led multinational investigations into crypto-laundering networks and dark web marketplaces.

    According to O’Neill, fraudsters are winning because fraud has evolved into a highly organized industry. He explained that scam operations now function much like large multinational corporations. Scam compounds are similar to call centers, complete with organizational structures, performance quotas, shift schedules and human resources departments. Unfortunately, many of these compounds operate under sophisticated criminal networks and employ workers who have been trafficked.

    Sources indicate that at the same time, the barrier to entry into the fraud world has never been lower. AI enables fraudsters to create convincing scams at scale in virtually any language, including cloned voices, deepfake videos and personalized social engineering campaigns. And it’s cheap.​.

    According to recent reports, the consequences of eroding trust extend well beyond fraud losses. Organizations often experience:.

    • Reduced marketing effectiveness.

    Ironically, the industries and brands most trusted by consumers are frequently among the most targeted by fraudsters, with the highest fraud instances related to auto lending, bank-issued and retail credit cards and unsecured personal lending.

    According to recent reports, according to Edelman, trust now rivals price and quality as a primary factor influencing consumer decision-making. Research highlights that “77% of consumers cited confidence their personal data is secure as the most important feature when choosing whom to transact with online.”.

    Organizations can strengthen trust by approaching fraud prevention and customer communications as a unified strategy.

    In a recent development, traditional fraud controls were designed for predictable attacks. Today’s fraudsters adapt quickly, vary their tactics and coordinate attacks across multiple channels and sessions. Identity verification remains vital, but it only confirms who someone claims to be. It doesn’t determine whether the current interaction should be trusted.

    Here’s where identity verification falls short:.

    • KYC (Know Your Customer) controls are often strongest at onboarding, not throughout the customer lifecycle.

    • Devices, behaviors and risk profiles change over time.

    • Credentials can be compromised after verification.

    • Synthetic identities can appear legitimate on paper.

    Recent findings suggest that the most important fraud signal is often not a single event. Any single signal can be manipulated or generate false positives. It’s the story that unfolds throughout an interaction. It emerges through relationships among consumers, devices, accounts, entities and sessions.

    As if it wasn’t hard enough, AI has turbocharged fraud. In addition, labeling identified threats as AI-driven remains a challenge. That’s because it’s difficult to build comprehensive strategies with fresh AI fraud models evolving so rapidly.

    Sources indicate that while fraud practitioners know when an account was taken over, there’s right now no label for how it was taken over and whether AI drove the attack. As a result, the AI-attributed training set doesn’t exist yet for tracking that fraud, and detection stays anchored to heuristics and analyst judgment.

    To be able to engage effectively with consumers and prevent fraud, organizations must adopt continuous authentication and layered risk strategies.

    • Develop a comprehensive strategy—don’t address fraud in silos across your organization.

    • Form strategic partnerships with your cyber teams.

    • Correlate identity, device, behavioral and contextual signals in real time.

    It has been revealed that the process is straightforward: Collect. Correlate. Score. Decide.

    Every phone call, text message, email and digital transaction represents a trust moment. Customers want confidence the organization contacting them is legitimate and their information and transactions are protected. Simply asking consumers to “trust us” is no longer enough.

    Verified identity, authenticated communications and real-time risk intelligence are becoming the foundation of trust in a digital-first world.

    In a recent development, the future isn’t reactive fraud mitigation. It’s proactive trust at the point of interaction, by orchestrating identity, risk and communications intelligence across every customer interaction.

    10 stocks we like better than Nabors Industries ›.

    On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Nabors Industries (NBR -6.47%) reported third-quarter adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) of $246 million. Higher fleet utilization and disciplined debt reduction give the company clear financial flexibility to expand internationally without overextending its balance sheet.

    Three things management said stand out.

    Transferring unassigned drilling equipment from North America to expanding international fields lets the organization secure long-term contracts without buying latest hardware. This rotation strategy increases earnings on existing equipment without demanding capital expenditure.

    In a recent development, operational gains and higher technology adoption are boosting margins despite operational frictions in the Middle East. High fleet utilization, deep client relationships, and automated technology give the organization clear competitive scale. Management focuses on pricing discipline and contract coverage.

    Falling interest costs and disciplined capital allocation position the manufacturer for sustainable growth.

    • The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.

    The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.

    The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.

    Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown has claimed that Liverpool sporting director Julian Ward has already decided that the club’s longest-serving current player won’t be offered a new deal, with injury issues not helping the defender’s case.

    He told Football Insider: “Liverpool have already decided they’re going to let Joe Gomez leave. He doesn’t have much of a role to play at the moment, he’s not starting games at right-back even despite their injuries, and he isn’t competing for a centre-back position.

    “His injuries are always a concern as well. They don’t think he can start games consistently, and all of these issues stack up eventually.

    “It would be a surprise to me if they were to offer him a fresh contract, especially when you consider they’re going to be looking to bring in new defenders at some stage.

    “If he hasn’t played much this season, that’s not going to change with new players coming in, so I expect he’ll be allowed to look at what other options might be available.”.

    Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Ward could be quite busy with contract renewals over the next few months, with Alisson Becker, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister reportedly all in line for prospective newly introduced deals.

    Whereas that trio are virtually guaranteed to start, though, Gomez usually has to rely on substitute appearances or heavy squad rotation for domestic cup games, and it’s not implausible that he could be allowed to depart on a free transfer next summer.

    If that is indeed his fate, he’ll be assured of a raucous send-off at Anfield on the final day of the season, with his popularity among the fan base unmistakably evident by the roar which greeted his successful penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout triumph over Chelsea last month.

    As Lewis Steele rightly noted, the 29-year-old ‘very rarely puts a foot wrong’ whenever he’s called upon, and even if he isn’t getting much game-time, we don’t doubt that he’s imparting some invaluable advice to the young defenders at Liverpool who can learn so much from him.

    Industry observers note that if this is to be Gomez’s last campaign with the Reds, all we ask is that he does finally, finally get his first goal for the club during regulation time. You’d be very hard pressed to find a more popular goalscorer if that moment were to happen!

    • Cryptocurrency markets suffered another brutal sell-off on Friday, November 20, as a wave of selling across Wall Street spilled into digital assets.
    • As of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -5.53%) had plunged 6.01% to $58,186.39, while Ethereum (ETH -6.15%) tumbled 9.03% to $1,596.72 and Solana (SOL -6.26%) declined 8.02% to $67.21.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By RJ Fulton – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:45PM EST.

    Cryptocurrency markets suffered another brutal sell-off on Friday, November 20, as a wave of selling across Wall Street spilled into digital assets. Bitcoin broke below the psychologically important $60,000 level, while Ethereum and Solana experienced even steeper declines as investors continued to retreat from riskier assets.

    As of early evening, Bitcoin (BTC -5.53%) had plunged 6.01% to $58,186.39, while Ethereum (ETH -6.15%) tumbled 9.03% to $1,596.72 and Solana (SOL -6.26%) declined 8.02% to $67.21. The latest losses come as major cryptocurrencies struggle to establish a bottom, with weakening liquidity and persistent selling pressure raising the prospect of fresh bear market lows.

    In a recent development, deteriorating investor risk appetite continued to weigh on cryptocurrencies Friday as concerns over interest rates, elevated valuations, and tighter financial conditions fueled a broad sell-off across global markets. With the Nasdaq plunging more than 5%, investors appeared increasingly focused on raising cash and reducing exposure to riskier assets.

    The simultaneous decline in stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies suggests selling pressure is extending beyond individual markets. Rather than simply rotating capital between asset classes, investors appear to be reducing their overall risk exposure, leaving cryptocurrencies particularly vulnerable as liquidity conditions continue to deteriorate.

    According to recent reports, spot cryptocurrency ETFs suffered steep losses on Friday, mirroring the broader sell-off in digital assets. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT -5.87%) fell 5.87%, while the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC -6.16%) declined 5.97%. Meanwhile, the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA -9.16%) plunged 9.16%, reflecting Ethereum's particularly sharp decline.

    Bitcoin's break below $60,000 marks another significant deterioration in the cryptocurrency market's technical outlook. With Ethereum approaching $1,500 and Solana falling below $70, several major cryptocurrencies are now trading near levels that could determine whether the current bear market extends into 2027. If selling pressure persists, investors could see another round of new lows before a sustainable recovery takes shape.

    Beyond price action, the broader withdrawal of capital from digital assets presents a more fundamental challenge. Bitcoin ETF outflows have reportedly exceeded $2.5 billion in 2026, while the simultaneous sell-off across stocks, gold, and cryptocurrencies suggests investors are prioritizing liquidity over risk-taking. Without renewed capital inflows, even sharp relief rallies may struggle to develop into sustained recoveries.

    Sources indicate that looking ahead, investors should watch whether Bitcoin can reclaim $60,000, Ethereum can recover above $1,800, and Solana can establish support above $70. Improving ETF flows, stabilizing prices, and a recovery in broader financial markets would provide more convincing evidence that conditions are improving. Until then, the combination of weakening demand and unfavorable macroeconomic conditions leaves cryptocurrencies vulnerable to further declines heading into year-end.

    Brandon Ingram expected to make season debut for Clippers on Monday vs. Rockets

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (445 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brandon Ingram is expected to make his 2026-27 season debut for the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
    • Before opening training camp, the Clippers announced that Ingram had been diagnosed with a partially torn Achilles tendon in his right leg.
    • That heel injury caused Ingram to miss Games 6 and 7 of the Toronto Raptors' first-round playoff defeat to the Cleveland Cavaliers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brandon Ingram is expected to make his 2026-27 season debut for the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

    Before opening training camp, the Clippers announced that Ingram had been diagnosed with a partially torn Achilles tendon in his right leg. The partial tear was discovered while the two-time All-Star underwent surgery to remove a bone spur from his right heel in May.

    That heel injury caused Ingram to miss Games 6 and 7 of the Toronto Raptors' first-round playoff defeat to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

    Ingram was traded by Toronto to the Clippers as part of a package including Gradey Dick, unprotected 2031 and 2033 first-round selections, a 2027 first-round swap and second-round picks in 2030 and 2033 in exchange for Kawhi Leonard.

    According to recent reports, the deal was originally agreed upon in late June and expected to become official on July 6 when the NBA's moratorium on transactions ended. However, the trade was put on hold amid the NBA's investigation into the Clippers allegedly evading the league's salary cap while signing Leonard to a three-year, $103 million free-agent contract in July 2019.

    Both the Clippers and Raptors agreed that the trade wouldn't be completed until the league's probe was completed. The deal finally went through in mid-September, approximately two weeks before NBA teams opened their training camps.

    It has been revealed that the Clippers knew about Ingram's Achilles tear — repaired in the same procedure that removed his bone spur — before agreeing to the trade, according to interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden. Redden told reporters that Ingram would require about six fewer months of rehab with a partial tear and expected he would play for the Clippers this season.

    Recent findings suggest that ingram averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists for the Raptors last season after being acquired from the New Orleans Pelicans in early 2025. Shortly after joining Toronto, he signed a three-year, $120 million contract extension.

    Sources indicate that during his 10 NBA seasons, Ingram has averaged 19.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 4.2 assists while shooting 37% on 3-pointers. He was the Los Angeles Lakers' 2016 first-round pick (No. 2 overall) out of Duke. Ingram played three seasons for the Lakers before being traded to Fresh Orleans as part of a three-team deal that sent Anthony Davis to L.A.

    Recent findings suggest that without Ingram, the Clippers are off to a 4-10 start that currently has them as the third-worst team in the Western Conference. The team has also been without Bradley Beal (knee) and Jordan Miller (shoulder) during the opening weeks of the season.

    By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than NiSource ›.

    On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, NiSource (NI -0.63%) raised its long-term financial guidance while expanding its capital investment commitments. The utility is blending standard regulated energy distribution with power contracts for giant technology facilities.

    Three things management said stand out.

    Sources indicate that niSource signed a 20-year agreement with Microsoft, marking its fifth data center power contract across three technology giants. The projects run through Genco, the tech giant's power generation segment, and lower electricity bills for retail customers of NIPSCO, its electric utility subsidiary.

    Executive Vice President Shawn Anderson detailed a newly introduced seven-year spending forecast that dedicates $32 billion to core regulated utilities and $8 billion to data center generation. Management expects this capital deployment to support compound annual adjusted earnings per share, or net income divided by outstanding stock, growth of 10% to 11%.

    Utilities usually wait years to collect revenues on fresh construction, creating regulatory lag that drags on cash flows. NiSource uses forward-looking rate structures and tracker mechanisms, which are regulatory processes that let utilities recover specific investment costs swiftly, to streamline cash generation.

    Large technology companies are expanding heavily across Northern Indiana, where available land, water access, and fiber networks give NiSource an operational edge over surrounding power grids. Management is watching regulatory approval schedules and construction milestones to ensure projects open on time.

    The utility couples steady 6% to 8% earnings growth from its base gas and electric utilities with higher-margin growth from data center power contracts. That combination creates two complementary income streams that insulate shareholders from regulatory shifts in any single state.

    #50911. When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1311 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1311 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test new solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout.
    • In a recent development, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question.
    • A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test new solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout. But not every pilot warrants further investment, and knowing when to end one can be just as vital as knowing when to expand it.

    In a recent development, for tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council share warning signs that indicate it’s time to end a technology pilot rather than extend it, redesign it or move it into production.

    A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot. Defining boundaries and expectations, and, importantly, being transparent, are critical to a pilot’s success. Customers should also share any uncertainty during the pilot instead of waiting for it to pivot or improve. - Arunava Sen, Tata Communications America Inc.

    A clear sign is when the pilot team cannot tell you what the technology accessed, what decisions it made, or what data it touched. If you cannot answer those questions in a controlled environment (test group), you will not answer them in production. - Michael Nicosia, Salt Security.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    In a recent development, one sign a technology pilot shouldn’t progress doesn’t involve the latest tech itself but the tools teams already work with. If teams are working in siloed workflows with tools that don’t collaborate with one another, introducing new technology can drive up costs, increase complexity and hurt productivity. Connected tools and workflows are integral to the success of any new tech deployment. - Usman Shuja, Bluebeam.

    End a pilot when its success depends on hand-curated data that won’t exist in production. If someone cleaned the dataset, resolved definitions and fixed edge cases for the pilot, and no one owns doing that at scale in production, extending or redesigning the product in production won’t help. In many cases, technology isn’t the problem; the foundation is. Ask not whether the pilot worked, but what it worked on. - Prakash Reddy, Okta.

    In a recent development, if the pilot only works while its champion is in the room or while the vendor quietly does manual work behind the scenes, you’ve tested enthusiasm, not technology. Hand it to a team that didn’t build it for 30 days. If results collapse, you’d be pushing a dependency into production, not a tool. End it and keep the learnings. - Damian Wasserman, BEON.tech.

    It has been revealed that when the team stops asking what we learned and starts asking when we get to stop, that’s the sign. A pilot without defined success criteria is avoidance. If you can’t name the specific business result it was supposed to prove or disprove, extending it won’t help. End it, define the outcome you actually need, and redesign around that from the start. - Ali Alkhafaji, APPLY.

    Organizations should end a technology pilot when they have full visibility of the tool’s usage and cost metrics but still cannot connect either to a meaningful business outcome. Adoption alone is not enough without a clear path to measurable value, and extending the pilot risks turning experimentation into ongoing spend without a business case. - Conal Gallagher, Flexera.

    A clear sign is when the people who were supposed to benefit stop asking about it. Pilots drag on because the sponsors like the idea, not because users need it. If the pilot group has quietly gone back to their old way of working and nobody complains when the tool goes down, there’s nothing to extend. Name the lesson, thank the team and end it. - Hastimal Jangid, Coozmoo Digital Solutions, Inc.

    Recent findings suggest that A pilot should be reconsidered when it performs well in a demo but can’t prove that it solves a real business problem. AI makes it easy to add capabilities, but more features don’t always mean more value. Teams need clear measures of success and feedback loops to understand what’s working and what’s not before investing further. - Tony Grout, M-Files.

    Sources indicate that A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when it repeatedly fails to demonstrate measurable business value despite validated assumptions and reasonable adjustments. If the solution cannot deliver meaningful ROI, operational efficiency or strategic impact, extending it only increases sunk costs. Strong leadership means knowing when to stop, not just when to scale. - Kameshwar Singh, Cohesity.

    End a pilot if no effort was spent defining the vision and how value will be realized at scale. That’s like building a bridge from both ends without deciding where it should meet. - Venky Ramesh, LatentView Analytics.

    A pilot should end when success depends on conditions that production will never have: handpicked data, expert customers, manual fixes, privileged integrations or constant vendor support. If removing that scaffolding collapses the value case, extending the pilot only perfects the illusion. The real test is not, “Does it work?” but, “Does it still create measurable value when exposed to ordinary users, messy data, real constraints and an ordinary day?” - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

    In a recent development, end a pilot when making the technology operable, reliable and governable outweighs its business value. If protecting sensitive data, maintaining an audit trail and providing human oversight would cost more than the expected benefit, extending that particular pilot needs a stronger business case than the time and money already invested. - Brian Stimpfl, S-Docs.

    End a pilot when the evidence invalidates its core business premise. If owners can complete the workflow but gain no meaningful time, cost or quality improvement over the current process, more engineering won’t create demand. Define that minimum benefit before launch, test it with real users, and stop when it remains out of reach. - Irina Shymko, Langate Software.

    End the pilot when the team cannot define a credible path from the experiment to a measurable business outcome. If success still depends on vague future improvements, heroic manual support or assumptions the pilot was supposed to validate, extending it usually just delays the decision. - Dhyey Mavani, Abridge.

    Recent findings suggest that A pilot should end when the team cannot explain what fresh evidence another extension will produce. Every extra week should answer a specific open question about value, risk, adoption, cost or scale. Once the remaining time is only keeping the pilot alive, the experiment has already delivered its answer. - Sibasis Padhi, Walmart Inc.

    Industry observers note that I would end a pilot when it successfully completes individual tasks but repeatedly fails to deliver the full business outcome. Often, the underlying matter is the absence of a clear decision model for handling exceptions, approvals or unresolved work across teams. If nobody can authorize what happens next, scaling the technology only scales the problem. - Vamshi Noothi, Cisco.

    Sources indicate that A pilot should be ended if nobody uses it unless someone reminds them. A pilot that only stays alive while its sponsor keeps pushing won’t survive production, and extending it just postpones that answer. Software nobody uses isn’t free; it still costs money to run, maintain and support. End it, write down what you learned about the problem, and put the team on something people actually want. - Jeremy Suriel, Kustomer.

    A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when no business owner is willing to take responsibility for implementation. Even if the technology performs well, success requires business ownership, accountability and commitment to change. Without a sponsor willing to champion the solution, allocate resources and own the outcomes, extending the pilot is unlikely to deliver value. Technology cannot create lasting benefits without clear business ownership. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

    • That massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market.
    • Industry observers note that an easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:55PM EST.

    Recent findings suggest that when SpaceX (SPCX -7.69%) went public in June, it disclosed $2.8 billion in purchase commitments for gas turbines and related equipment in its IPO prospectus. SpaceX is purchasing those turbines to power its own data centers and factories.

    That massive investment in behind-the-meter (BTM) natural gas connections, which generate electricity on the customer's side of the electric meter rather than going through an energy provider, is a bright green flag for the natural gas market. U.S. data centers already generate over 40% of their electricity from natural gas, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). That percentage could continue to rise as the cloud and AI markets expand.

    Industry observers note that an easy way to profit from that secular trend is through midstream pipeline companies, which deliver the natural gas to those data centers. Pipeline operators charge companies "tolls" to use their infrastructure, so they're well-insulated from volatile commodity prices. Instead, they simply need the resources to keep flowing through their pipes to generate stable profits. Most pipeline companies also return lots of cash to their investors through high dividends and distributions.

    According to recent reports, as demand for natural gas rises, pipeline companies will need to expand their infrastructure to handle the increased volumes. Those investments could compress their near-term margins, but they'll support their long-term growth. Let's see which of these pipeline operators will benefit the most from the rapid growth of the cloud infrastructure and AI data center markets.

    In a recent development, the Williams Companies (WMB -2.75%) operates more than 32,000 miles of pipeline across 24 states. It owns Transco, the largest natural gas pipeline in the U.S., which connects the Gulf Coast to the Atlantic seaboard. Its pipelines handle roughly a third of all natural gas produced in the United States.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Unlike more diversified pipeline companies, Williams generates most of its revenue by gathering, processing, storing, and transporting natural gas. A smaller percentage of revenue comes from natural gas liquids (NGLs), crude oil handling services, and electricity generation.

    According to recent reports, from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Williams' EPS to grow at a 12% CAGR. It still looks reasonably valued at 26 times next year's earnings, and it could command an even higher valuation if the data center market heats up again.

    Williams has raised its dividend annually over the past nine years, and it's paid continuous dividends for the past 52 years. It currently pays a forward yield of 3.2%, and its low payout ratio of 82% gives it ample room for future dividend hikes.

    Recent findings suggest that energy Transfer (ET -2.62%) operates more than 140,000 miles of pipeline across 44 states. It transports crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), and other refined products through its pipelines. It also exports NGLs through its marine export terminals.

    TXSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Energy Transfer's pipelines transport about 30% of the natural gas produced in the United States. It generates only approximately 40% of its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) from natural gas, which makes it less of a direct play on natural gas than Williams. Still, Energy Transfer is more exposed to that market than many of its peers.

    Unlike Williams, which operates as a traditional corporation, Energy Transfer is a master limited partnership (MLP) that treats its investors as partners rather than shareholders. MLPs pay distributions -- much of which are classified as a "return of capital" for more tax-efficient returns -- rather than traditional dividends. That strategy enables it to pay a high forward yield of 7.2%, but its investors must file an additional K-1 form (for MLPs) with their taxes each year.

    Recent findings suggest that from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Energy Transfer's earnings per unit (EPU) to grow at a 13% CAGR. It trades at just 12 times next's year's EPU, and that low valuation should limit its downside even if the cloud and AI markets cool off over the next few years.

    Credo Technology Group vs. Western Digital: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:57PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Credo Technology Group ›.
    • The race for faster data processing is pushing infrastructure to its limits, forcing a choice between specialized connectivity and massive storage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Credo Technology Group ›.

    The race for faster data processing is pushing infrastructure to its limits, forcing a choice between specialized connectivity and massive storage. You might be deciding between Credo Technology Group (CRDO -15.20%) and Western Digital (WDC -12.02%) for 2027.

    Credo provides high-speed connectivity solutions that enable artificial intelligence data centers to communicate efficiently, while Western Digital is a global leader in both hard disk and flash storage. While they operate in different niches, both are essential players in the scaling of cloud infrastructure. This comparison evaluates which stock offers the best path for long-term growth.

    Credo Technology Group specializes in high-speed copper and optical interconnect solutions designed for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company sells products like Active Electrical Cables and optical components to hyperscale operators and system vendors. It has established key partnerships with Oracle (ORCL -8.48%) and Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) to enhance connectivity for dual-architecture systems.

    In a recent development, the demand for faster semiconductor stocks has significantly boosted its financial performance. In the 12 months ended Aug. 1, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.6 billion, representing a 165.1% increase over the previous period. This expansion led to a net income of roughly $538.3 million and a net margin of about 33.8%.

    According to recent reports, as of its May 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, meaning the firm carries no debt relative to shareholder equity. Its current ratio is approximately 10.2x, indicating a strong ability to cover short-term debts with current assets. In the fiscal year ended May 2, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $407.0 million, though stock-based compensation represented roughly 39.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Sources indicate that western Digital designs and supplies essential data-storage solutions for enterprises and hyperscale cloud providers. Its product portfolio includes both hard disk drives and flash-based storage serving a global market across Asia and the Americas. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk, with three individual clients accounting for 16%, 15%, and 13% of total net revenue in its latest annual report.

    In the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $14.5 billion, representing a 43% increase compared to the prior year. Net income for this period was nearly $10.0 billion, which indicates a net margin of roughly 69.2%. This performance suggests a robust recovery in cloud storage demand, which now accounts for nearly 89% of its net revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that on its July 2026 balance sheet, the firm indicates a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.1x, meaning total debt is low relative to equity. The current ratio stands at approximately 1.3x, measuring how well the company meets its short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended July 3, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $3.5 billion, representing operating cash flow minus capital expenditures.

    Recent findings suggest that credo Technology Group faces intense competition from larger industry peers like Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%), Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%), and Astera Labs (ALAB -14.77%). The organization also deals with geopolitical risks due to its reliance on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for all semiconductor manufacturing. Furthermore, it manages previously flagged intellectual property litigation with Marvell Technology, which was recently resolved via a settlement.

    According to recent reports, western Digital must navigate risks associated with its complex strategic initiatives, such as the 2025 separation of its former flash business unit. It competes directly with other storage manufacturers like Seagate Technology Holdings (STX -12.35%) and providers of alternative storage technologies. Additionally, the firm relies on a limited supply base for critical components, leaving it exposed to potential global supply chain disruptions.

    Western Digital is cheaper, trading at a lower Forward P/E for future earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio based on sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with Credo Technology, a company whose sales have more than doubled year over year for seven straight quarters. AI data centers run on thousands of chips that need to share data promptly, and Credo is a key player that makes the connections between them.

    It has been revealed that management expects sales to grow more than 85% this fiscal year, and Credo is also very profitable, turning about half of its sales into adjusted profit. It's also moving into optical products that carry data farther than its copper cables can, and management expects them to bring in more than $600 million this fiscal year. The stock fell after its recent earnings report, as investors worried that a few big customers make up most of its sales, but Credo added another big customer in its latest quarter.

    To its credit, Western Digital's hard drives store much of the data AI creates, and its profit has jumped. But rival Toshiba is reportedly doubling its hard drive capacity, which could pull prices down. For long-term investors, Credo pairs fast growth with strong profits, and it has a front-row seat as AI data centers get bigger. With plenty of cash on hand, it can keep investing in new products for years to come.

    Breaking: Is Coca-Cola a Millionaire-Maker Stock?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (720 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that few businesses exemplify American business success more than Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%).
    • Industry observers note that over the last 12 months alone, shares have jumped by an impressive 35%, substantially outpacing the S&P 500's return of just 8% over the same time frame.
    • To understand Coca-Cola's appeal, it can pay to listen to the philosophy of one of its biggest backers, Warren Buffett.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Ebiefung – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

    Recent findings suggest that few businesses exemplify American business success more than Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%). Since its founding in the late 19th century, the multinational beverage maker has expanded globally to serve billions and become one of the world's most recognized brands. Investors have profited substantially along the way, and this shows little sign of stopping.

    Industry observers note that over the last 12 months alone, shares have jumped by an impressive 35%, substantially outpacing the S&P 500's return of just 8% over the same time frame. This is a significant deal for a organization that is already large and mature. Let's dig deeper into the pros and cons of Coca-Cola to decide if the company still has millionaire-maker potential.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    To understand Coca-Cola's appeal, it can pay to listen to the philosophy of one of its biggest backers, Warren Buffett. His Berkshire Hathaway portfolio owns a whopping $38.4 billion worth of Coca-Cola stock, making it his third-largest bet behind American Express and Apple.

    Buffett likes to invest in companies with simple and easy-to-understand business models that enjoy a strong economic moat. A moat is a competitive advantage that protects a company's market share against competition and allows it to enjoy stable or elevated pricing power. Coca-Cola is arguably the quintessential example of this type of business.

    You can walk into a convenience store or restaurant practically anywhere in the world and find Coca-Cola's flagship beverage Coke (or one of its many subbrands like Sprite, Fanta, and a variety of localized options).

    According to recent reports, the company's ubiquitous shelf space has created unparalleled habit creation among its consumers, which is something latest rivals will struggle to disrupt, even if they manage to create better-tasting products. This advantage also makes Coca-Cola's sales remarkably recession-resistant. It has allowed the company to protect its margins amid soaring global inflation in raw materials like aluminum and sugar.

    Coca-Cola's gross margins have hovered around 60%, despite the soaring prices for its products. This suggests the company is passing on the vast majority of inflation to consumers, while protecting its own profitability.

    KO Gross Profit Margin data by YCharts.

    Industry observers note that coca-Cola isn't without some long-term challenges. The tech giant is already a global brand name, and that means there is very little room for organic growth. Management will be increasingly tempted to rely on price increases to juice investor returns. While the company's gross margin of over 60% was easy to justify back when a 12-pack cost $4.00, it is much harder to stomach when prices have doubled, and more American families are struggling to make ends meet.

    According to recent reports, soda prices have far exceeded the U.S. inflation rate, despite boasting a disproportionately middle- and lower-income consumer base. It's hard not to wonder if this situation is as sustainable as it may look on the surface.

    Over the long term, there could be a generational shift away from brand-name soft drinks as people become more comfortable buying lower-cost store brands from major retailers like Walmart, which offers alternatives like Sam's Cola and Twist Up.

    It has been revealed that coca-Cola's recent performance is impressive, and its strong moat can help set the company up for more market-beating growth over the long term. That said, with a market cap of $422 billion (in a mature industry with relatively little room for organic growth), Coca-Cola's days of explosive millionaire-making growth are likely behind it. Shares are also somewhat expensive at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 28.

    Investors who buy the stock now should look at it as a safer alternative to more speculative opportunities like generative AI. The manufacturer's dividend (at the moment boasting a yield of 2.21%) will likely represent a sizable percentage of its long-term returns.
